b.t_id: Kata kerja: kata kerja modal (Modalverben)
Makna

b.t: While verbs are used to describe actions, modal verbs add to the meaning by providing some nuance or by suggesting some emotional reaction to an action. Consider the following English examples:
b.t_id: Kata kerja dipakai untuk menggambarkan tindakan, sedangkan kata kerja modal menambah makna dengan memberi nuansa atau menyiratkan sikap terhadap suatu tindakan. Perhatikan contoh berikut:

b.t: The good girl spins at the well. The good girl must spin at the well. The good girl should spin at the well.
b.t_id: Gadis baik itu memintal di sumur. Gadis baik itu harus memintal di sumur. Gadis baik itu sebaiknya memintal di sumur.

b.t: In the first sentence, the girl is actually spinning thread right now. In the second one, she must spin because somebody demands it of her (but she may or may not be spinning right now). The third sentence indicates that she has a duty that she is apparently rejecting for something more exciting ...
b.t_id: Dalam kalimat pertama, gadis itu sedang memintal benang saat ini. Dalam kalimat kedua, ia harus memintal karena seseorang menuntutnya (tetapi belum tentu ia sedang memintal sekarang). Kalimat ketiga menunjukkan bahwa ia punya kewajiban yang tampaknya ia tolak demi sesuatu yang lebih menarik ...

b.t: Thus, modal verbs modify other verbs. They are followed by an infinitive (the basic form of a verb, what you would find in the dictionary).
b.t_id: Jadi, kata kerja modal mengubah makna kata kerja lain. Kata kerja modal diikuti infinitif (bentuk dasar kata kerja, yang Anda temukan di kamus).
Kata kerja modal

b.t: There are six – or seven – modal verbs in German: dürfen, können, mögen (+möchten), müssen, sollen, wollen
b.t_id: Ada enam – atau tujuh – kata kerja modal dalam bahasa Jerman: dürfen, können, mögen (+möchten), müssen, sollen, wollen

b.t: 1. dürfen • be allowed to, be permitted to
Be aware that the negative of dürfen really means "must not" or "may not" (it is a prohibition).
b.t_id: Perhatikan bahwa bentuk negatif dürfen benar-benar berarti „tidak boleh“ (sebuah larangan).

r: Eine Witwe hat zwei Töchter: Die eine ist verwöhnt und die andere darf nichts tun außer arbeiten.
A widow has two daughters: one is spoiled, the other one is only allowed to work.
Eines Tages wird ihr Finger vom Spinnen blutig sein, aber sie darf mit der Arbeit nicht aufhören.
One day her finger gets bloody from the spinning, but she is not allowed to stop working.
Tja, das ist leider das Schicksal von allen Waisen in diesen Märchen; sie dürfen am Anfang der Geschichte nicht glücklich sein!
Oh well, that is unfortunately the fate of all orphans in these fairy tales; they are not allowed to be happy at the beginning of the story!

ja: 同情, 仕方がない

b.t: Although in American English 'can' is often used interchangeably with 'allowed to' ('Mom, can we go home now?'), in German the meaning of these two words are distinct. dürfen indicates the permission to do something, können means the ability/skill to do something.
b.t_id: Dalam bahasa Indonesia „bisa“ sering dipakai untuk „boleh“ („Bu, kami bisa pulang sekarang?“), tetapi dalam bahasa Jerman maknanya berbeda tegas. dürfen menyatakan izin melakukan sesuatu, können berarti kemampuan/keterampilan melakukan sesuatu.

r: Die Spule wird auch blutig, aber das Mädchen kann sie nicht waschen, weil der Brunnen zu tief ist.
The spool gets bloody too, but the girl can not wash it because the well is too deep.
Aber was zunächst passiert, kann ich gar nicht verstehen: Die Stiefmutter sagt dem Mädchen, dass sie in den Brunnen springen und die Spule zurückbringen muss.
But I can not understand at all what happens next: the stepmother tells the girl that she has to jump in the well and bring back the spool.

b.t: mögen means to like ... Unlike the other modal verbs, it is not used to modify a verb; rather, it's used with nouns: Ich mag Tee lieber als Kaffee (I like tea better than coffee). These nouns have to be in the accusative. To negate mögen, you need to use kein/keine with a noun and nicht if you are negating the mögen itself.
b.t_id: mögen berarti suka ... Berbeda dengan kata kerja modal lain, mögen tidak dipakai untuk mengubah makna kata kerja; ia dipakai dengan kata benda: Ich mag Tee lieber als Kaffee (Saya lebih suka teh daripada kopi). Kata bendanya harus dalam akusatif. Untuk menegasikan mögen, pakai kein/keine dengan kata benda dan nicht bila menegasikan mögen itu sendiri.

r: Why don't you guys like me?
Wir mögen keine Waisen, weil wir böse sind. So muss das sein, um unser Märchen bedeutungsvoll zu machen.
We don't like orphans because we are evil. It has to be that way, in order to make our tale meaningful.

継母, 義母

b.t: möchten is not really a full-blown modal verb; it is a form of mögen (the subjunctive form) and is used for a softer version of like – namely, it means would like. mögen is used with verbs or with nouns. The nouns are in the accusative here, too.
b.t_id: möchten sebenarnya bukan kata kerja modal penuh; ia bentuk dari mögen (bentuk konjungtif) dan dipakai untuk „suka“ yang lebih halus – yaitu „ingin / mau“. möchten dipakai dengan kata kerja atau kata benda. Kata bendanya di sini juga dalam akusatif.

b.t: Two additional, useful expressions: möchte gern (would really like to ...) and möchte lieber (would prefer to ...)
b.t_id: Dua ungkapan tambahan yang berguna: möchte gern (sangat ingin ...) dan möchte lieber (lebih suka ...)

r: Ich glaube, ich möchte lieber in ein anderes Märchen umziehen.
I think, I would really prefer to move to another fairy tale.
Ich glaube, du möchtest in den anderen Geschichten auch nicht sein. Sie sind alle etwas grausam und moralistisch übertrieben.
I believe that you wouldn't like the other stories either. They are all a bit dreadful and excessively moralistic.
Ja, aber einmal möchte ich das gerne ausprobieren!
Yeah, but at least once I'd really like to try it!

継母, 義母
はい, ええ

b.t: müssen means the same as the English must in positive (declarative) sentences and in questions. However, when you negate it and say müssen nicht, it is not the same as the English must not (which really means that you are not supposed to or not allowed to something => in German means "dürfen nicht"). Rather, it means that you do not have to do something. In other words:
b.t_id: müssen berarti „harus“ dalam kalimat positif (pernyataan) dan kalimat tanya. Namun saat dinegasikan menjadi müssen nicht, artinya bukan „tidak boleh“ (itu dalam bahasa Jerman „dürfen nicht“), melainkan Anda tidak harus melakukan sesuatu. Dengan kata lain:

r: you do not have to (≠ you must not)
you must not (you may not, you are not allowed)
Also, wo waren wir? Ach ja, du musst in den Brunnen hineinspringen und deine Spule zurückbringen!
So, where were we? Oh, yeah, you must jump into the well and bring your spool back!
Schade! Aber wenn ich ertrinke, muss ich wenigstens nicht mehr spinnen!
Bummer! But if I drown, at least I don't have to spin anymore.

ja: ～もまた, また
少女、女の子, 家事手伝い。女中。メイド, 少女

b.t: sollen does not really mean the same as should, such as in "you should really be happy that you jumped into the well!" Rather, sollen indicates an expectation or a duty or an obligation.
b.t_id: sollen tidak benar-benar sama dengan „sebaiknya“, seperti dalam „kamu sebaiknya senang sudah melompat ke sumur!“. sollen menyatakan harapan, tugas atau kewajiban (dari orang lain).

b.t: The more general English should can be expressed in a variety of ways in German: Ach, nimm uns doch aus dem Ofen! (oh, you should really take us out of the oven!) or Sie müsste viel mehr arbeiten! (she should work much more!). müsste is in the subjunctive, and the subjunctive form of sollen (sollte, solltest, etc.) can also mean should in the more everyday sense, as it is used in English.
b.t_id: Makna „sebaiknya“ yang lebih umum bisa dinyatakan dengan berbagai cara dalam bahasa Jerman: Ach, nimm uns doch aus dem Ofen! (ayo, keluarkanlah kami dari oven!) atau Sie müsste viel mehr arbeiten! (ia seharusnya bekerja jauh lebih banyak!). müsste adalah bentuk konjungtif, dan bentuk konjungtif sollen (sollte, solltest, dst.) juga bisa berarti „sebaiknya“ dalam pengertian sehari-hari.

r: Halloooo! Jemand soll uns aus dem Ofen herausholen!
Helloooo! Somebody is supposed to take us out of the oven!
Ja, ich glaube, dass ich das tun soll.
Yes, I believe that I am the one who is supposed to do that.
Richtig. Nach dem Drehbuch sollen wir nur im zweiten Akt im Ofen bleiben und verkohlen.
Yes, according to the screen-play, we are only supposed to be left burning in the oven in act two.

ja: はい, ええ

b.t: wollen is pretty straightforward, and means the same – and is used the same way – as the English equivalent want to. The only difficulty that sometimes arises is in its singular forms, which look deceptively like the English will (as in "sometime in the future I will return to Frau Holle"). The German wollen, in no shape or form, is used to form the future tense! In other words:
b.t_id: wollen cukup lugas, artinya „mau / ingin“. Satu-satunya kesulitan yang kadang muncul adalah bentuk tunggalnya (will), yang mirip kata Inggris „will“ untuk masa depan. wollen dalam bahasa Jerman sama sekali tidak dipakai untuk membentuk kala mendatang! Dengan kata lain:

r: Ich will zu Frau Holle zurückgehen.
I want to return to Frau Holle.
Ich werde zu Frau Holle zurückgehen.
I will return to Frau Holle.
Herzlich willkommen, liebes Kind! Wenn du bei mir bleiben willst, musst du aber sehr hart arbeiten!
Welcome, darling child! If you want to stay with me, however, you really have to work hard!
Ja, das will ich tun; das Leben hier ist viel gemütlicher als zu Hause, und ich arbeite gern!
Yes, that's what I want to do; life here is much cozier than at home, and I like to work!
Braves Mädchen! Ich mag deine protestantische Arbeitsmoral!
Good girl! I like your protestant work ethic!

b.t: Typically, the conjugated modal verb takes the second position in a sentence or clause, and an infinitive comes at the end of the sentence or clause.
b.t_id: Biasanya kata kerja modal yang dikonjugasikan menempati posisi kedua dalam kalimat atau anak kalimat, dan infinitif berada di akhir kalimat atau anak kalimat.

r: Tochter, du musst auch fortgehen und reich werden wie das andere Mädchen.
Daughter, you have to go out and become rich, like the other girl.
Ja, ich möchte sehr gern reich werden. Es ist nur so, dass ich nicht gern arbeite ...
Yes, I would very much like to become rich. It's only that I don't like to work so much ...

ja: 継母, 義母
はい, ええ

b.t_id: Bersama konjungsi koordinatif

b.t: This same pattern – conjugated modal verb in second position and infinitive at the end of a sentence or clause – holds true when two sentences (that become two clauses of a new, complex sentence) are connected by coordinating conjunctions: aber, beziehungsweise, denn, entweder ... oder ..., oder, sondern, und, weder ... noch ...
b.t_id: Pola yang sama – kata kerja modal terkonjugasi di posisi kedua dan infinitif di akhir kalimat atau anak kalimat – berlaku bila dua kalimat (yang menjadi dua klausa dari kalimat majemuk baru) dihubungkan dengan konjungsi koordinatif: aber, beziehungsweise, denn, entweder ... oder ..., oder, sondern, und, weder ... noch ...

r: Du musst zuerst drei Proben bestehen, und danach kannst du mit dem Gold nach Hause zurückkommen.
First, you have to pass three tests, and then you can come back home with the gold.

b.t_id: Bersama konjungsi subordinatif

b.t: The situation changes drastically with subordinating conjunctions, such as als, bevor, dass, ob, weil. Just as in other sentences with subordinating conjunctions, the conjugated verb (here the modal verb) goes to the end of the sentence or clause (the infinitive, which used to be at the end of the clause is now second-to-last, because the last slot is filled with the conjugated modal verb).
b.t_id: Keadaannya berubah drastis dengan konjungsi subordinatif, seperti als, bevor, dass, ob, weil. Seperti dalam kalimat lain dengan konjungsi subordinatif, kata kerja yang dikonjugasikan (di sini kata kerja modal) pindah ke akhir kalimat atau anak kalimat (infinitif yang tadinya di akhir anak kalimat kini menjadi kedua dari belakang, karena tempat terakhir diisi kata kerja modal yang dikonjugasikan).

r: Aber vergiss nicht, dass du alle drei Proben bestehen musst, bevor du das Gold bekommen kannst!
But don't forget that you have to pass all three tests before you can get the gold!
Weißt du zufällig, ob ich irgendwie mogeln kann?
Do you know if I can somehow cheat?

ja: 腹違い, 義理の姉妹

b.t_id: Kata kerja modal tanpa infinitif

b.t: As you already read above, the modal verb mögen is used without an infinitive, and its variant möchten can be used with nouns as well. However, there are some instances in which other modal verbs may go solo, too.
b.t_id: Seperti sudah Anda baca di atas, kata kerja modal mögen dipakai tanpa infinitif, dan variannya möchten juga bisa dipakai dengan kata benda. Namun ada beberapa keadaan di mana kata kerja modal lain juga bisa berdiri sendiri.
1. Kata kerja gerak yang sudah jelas

b.t: If the modal verb is used with a verb of motion, and an adverb of place already clearly indicates that motion, the infinitive can be left off:
b.t_id: Jika kata kerja modal dipakai bersama kata kerja gerak, dan keterangan tempat sudah jelas menunjukkan gerakan itu, infinitifnya boleh dihilangkan:

r: Ich will zu Frau Holle zurückkommen.
Ich will zurück zu Frau Holle.
Darf ich wieder nach Hause gehen?

b.t_id: 2. Kemampuan/keterampilan

b.t: You can leave off an infintive after können if the infinitive would be sprechen (to speak) and the object is the name of a language or tun (to do) and the object(s) make it clear that tun is the omitted element:
b.t_id: Anda boleh menghilangkan infinitif sesudah können jika infinitifnya sprechen (berbicara) dan objeknya nama bahasa, atau tun (melakukan) dan objeknya sudah jelas menunjukkan bahwa tun yang dihilangkan:

r: Frau Holle, können Sie Deutsch sprechen?
Ja, natürlich kann ich das tun!

b.t: Which of the following modal verbs best completes each sentence? Select the correct answers and find out more about the good girl's stay with Frau Holle. You really need to pay attention to the other clues in the sentence (e.g., a description of a person) to know whethter they 'have to' or 'want to' do something, for example!
b.t_id: Kata kerja modal mana yang paling tepat melengkapi setiap kalimat? Pilih jawaban yang benar dan ketahui lebih banyak tentang tinggalnya si gadis baik di rumah Frau Holle. Anda benar-benar perlu memperhatikan petunjuk lain dalam kalimat (mis. gambaran seseorang) untuk mengetahui apakah mereka „harus“ atau „ingin“ melakukan sesuatu!

Eines Tages wird ihre Hand blutig, aber sie _______ sie nicht waschen, weil der Brunnen zu tief ist.
Sie verliert ihre Spule, und _______ sie vom Brunnen zurückbringen.

Nach einer Weile hat sie aber Heimweh (she is homesick), und _______ wieder nach Hause.

b.t: Just as modal verbs do in the present tense, they also modify other verbs in the past tense as well; they provide some nuance or suggest some emotional reaction to an action.
b.t_id: Seperti dalam present, kata kerja modal juga mengubah makna kata kerja lain dalam bentuk lampau; kata ini memberi nuansa atau menyiratkan sikap terhadap suatu tindakan.

b.t: Thus, modal verbs modify other verbs. They are most often used along with an infinitive - the basic form of a verb, what you would find in the dictionary - which comes at the end of the sentence or the clause.
b.t_id: Jadi, kata kerja modal mengubah makna kata kerja lain. Kata kerja modal paling sering dipakai bersama infinitif – bentuk dasar kata kerja, yang Anda temukan di kamus – yang berada di akhir kalimat atau anak kalimat.

r: Also, fangen wir damit an, was wir in den alten Märchen machen durften ... und auch was wir nicht durften. Wer will beginnen?
So, let's begin with what we were allowed to do and also what we weren't allowed in the old fairy tales. Who wants to begin?
Damals durfte ich noch Kinder erschrecken und auffressen!!!
Back then I was still allowed to scare and eat children!!!

r: Tja, in den alten Zeiten konnte ich noch so richtig gut zaubern... Jetzt sind alle meine Versuche wie verhext!
Well, in the good old times I could still do some darned good magic ... Now, it seems like all my attempts are jinxed!
Ja, und die Prinzessinnen konnten meinem Charme gar nicht widerstehen ... Wenn doch nur die Gebrüder Grimm heute noch die Fäden in der Hand halten könnten!
Yeah, and the princesses could not resist my charm ... If only the Brothers Grimm were still at the helm today!

ja: はい, ええ

b.t: mögen and möchten only have one simple past form (because möchten is merely a form of mögen as well!). In the past tense, mögen can be used either with an infinitive or with a direct object.
b.t_id: mögen dan möchten hanya punya satu bentuk lampau sederhana (karena möchten pun hanyalah bentuk dari mögen!). Dalam bentuk lampau, mögen bisa dipakai dengan infinitif atau dengan objek langsung.

r: Mein Leben ist selbst heute noch dasselbe: Ich mochte damals niemanden, und ich mag heute auch keinen Menschen!
My life is still the same today: I didn't like anybody then, and I still don't like a single person today!

Ganz im Gegenteil, unser Leben ist völlig anders. Im originalen Märchen mochten wir es, im Bergbau zu arbeiten, aber heute finden wir das zu umweltfeindlich ... Oder haben wir nur in der Disneyversion so viel gesungen?

In total contrast, our life is completely different. In the original fairy tale, we liked to work in the mine, but today we find that too harmful for the environment ... Or did we only sing so much in the Disney version?

ja: 上司, チーフ, ボス

r: Wie Sie alle wissen, musste ich in einem Märchen der bösen Königin dienen! Ich habe das sooooo gehasst! (er schaudert und seufzt traurig)
As you all know, in one fairy tale I had to serve the evil queen! I really hated that! (he shivers and sighs sadly)
Man muss nichts müssen! Man muss sich immer selbst entscheiden, was man tun will ...
People did not have to do anything! You always have to determine for yourself what you want to do ...
Das ist doch alles Quatsch! Wir mussten alle machen, was die Gebrüder Grimm - und ehrlich gesagt, die deutsche Gesellschaft im 19. Jahrundert - uns vorgeschrieben hatte!
That's total nonsense! We all had to do what the Brothers Grimm - and in all honesty, the German society of the 19th century - dictated to us!

ja: 猟師, 戦闘機, 狩人
意地の悪い人

r: Ich sollte jeden Tag Frau Holles Bett aufschütteln, dann sollte es auf der Welt schneien.
I was supposed to shake up Frau Holle's bed every day, and then it was supposed to snow on Earth.

Das ist doch nichts! Ich sollte sterben! Mit 15!! Aber die 13. gute Weise konnte mein Todesurteil reduzieren, und ich musste nur 100 Jahre lang schlafen. Gott sei dank sollte damals das Gute immer siegen!

That's nothing! I was supposed to die! At age 15!! But the 13th wise woman could reduce my death sentence and I only had to sleep for 100 years. Thank heavens the Good was always supposed to win over evil back then!

ja: バラ, 眠れる森の美女, 小さい

r: Hänsel und Gretel, was wolltet ihr machen?
Hänsel und Gretel, what did you want to do?
Was für eine dumme Frage!?! Natürlich wollten wir zurück zu unserem Vater. Und ich wollte keinesfalls für eine alte Hexe das Mittagessen werden!
What a dumb question!?! Of course we wanted to get back to our father. And I by no means wanted to become lunch for an old hag!

I hated my fairy tale. I had to sort peas and lentils from the ashes every day. What an absolutely meaningless task!

b.t_id: Bersama konjungsi koordinatif

b.t: The same pattern - conjugated modal verb in second position and infinitive at the end of a sentence or clause - holds true when two sentences – that become two clauses of a new, complex sentence – are connected by coordinating conjunctions: aber, beziehungsweise, denn, entweder ... oder ..., oder, sondern, und, weder ... noch ...
b.t_id: Pola yang sama – kata kerja modal terkonjugasi di posisi kedua dan infinitif di akhir kalimat atau anak kalimat – berlaku bila dua kalimat – yang menjadi dua klausa dari kalimat majemuk baru – dihubungkan dengan konjungsi koordinatif: aber, beziehungsweise, denn, entweder ... oder ..., oder, sondern, und, weder ... noch ...

r: Ich war schon damals sehr alt. Ich musste von zu Hause weglaufen, denn ich konnte nicht mehr arbeiten. Sonst wäre ich ermordet worden!
I was already then very old. I had to run away from home, because I couldn't work around the house anymore. Otherwise I would have been murdered!

ja: 驢馬, 尻, お尻

b.t_id: Bersama konjungsi subordinatif

b.t: Just as with present tense modal verbs, the word order changes drastically with subordinating conjunctions, such as als, bevor, dass, ob, weil, for example. The conjugated verb (here, the modal verb) goes to the end of the sentence or clause with the subordinating conjunction.
b.t_id: Seperti kata kerja modal dalam present, susunan kata berubah drastis dengan konjungsi subordinatif, misalnya als, bevor, dass, ob, weil. Kata kerja yang dikonjugasikan (di sini kata kerja modal) pindah ke akhir kalimat atau anak kalimat yang memakai konjungsi subordinatif.

r: Ehrlich gesagt, es hat mir sehr gefallen, dass die Prinzessinnen mich in jedem Märchen küssen wollten. Naja, und heutzutage, mit diesem ganzen Feminismus ..., genug gesagt, finde ich.

b.t: In order to describe actions that happened in the past, you can use the so-called Perfekt tense, which is used in conversations or informal writing.
b.t_id: Untuk menggambarkan tindakan yang terjadi di masa lampau, Anda bisa memakai kala yang disebut Perfekt, yang dipakai dalam percakapan atau tulisan tidak resmi.

b.t: The Perfekt tense is sometimes also called Present Perfect, but this name is misleading for American learners, since the English present perfect (Wolfgang has not eaten Little Red Riding Hood) has a slightly different meaning from the basic past tense (Wolfgang did not eat Little Red Riding Hood). In the first case, he still has hope ... in the second one, a completed situation (opportunity lost) in the past is simply described. In German the Perfekt, for the most part, has the same meaning as the Simple Past:
b.t_id: Kala Perfekt kadang juga disebut Present Perfect, tetapi nama ini menyesatkan, karena present perfect dalam bahasa Inggris (Wolfgang has not eaten Little Red Riding Hood – Wolfgang belum memakan Si Kerudung Merah) maknanya sedikit berbeda dari lampau biasa (Wolfgang did not eat Little Red Riding Hood – Wolfgang tidak memakan Si Kerudung Merah). Dalam kasus pertama, ia masih punya harapan ... dalam kasus kedua, yang digambarkan hanyalah situasi yang sudah selesai (kesempatan hilang) di masa lampau. Dalam bahasa Jerman, Perfekt sebagian besar bermakna sama dengan lampau sederhana:

b.t: Wolfgang did not eat Little Red Riding Hood.

The Perfekt and the Simple Past forms are used in different types of interactions (informal/casual vs. formal). Sometimes the distinction is made between oral versus written use, but that is not quite accurate, because some types of writing are less formal (e.g., E-mail, a weblog) than some types of speaking (e.g., a formal lecture, accepting your Nobel prize, etc.). It is better to remember that the Perfekt is used for informal interaction, and Simple Past is more formal.
b.t_id: Bentuk Perfekt dan lampau sederhana dipakai dalam jenis interaksi yang berbeda (tidak resmi/santai dan resmi). Kadang pembedaannya disebut lisan dan tulis, tetapi itu kurang tepat, karena beberapa jenis tulisan kurang resmi (mis. surel, blog) dibandingkan beberapa jenis ucapan (mis. kuliah resmi, pidato penerimaan hadiah Nobel). Lebih baik diingat bahwa Perfekt dipakai untuk interaksi tidak resmi, dan lampau sederhana lebih resmi.

b.t: You can use any verb with the present perfect, but in High German (a type of "standard" German) some verbs are preferred in the simple past (and you might sound overly casual if you use these verbs with the Perfekt.
b.t_id: Kata kerja apa pun bisa dipakai dalam Perfekt, tetapi dalam bahasa Jerman baku beberapa kata kerja lebih disukai dalam lampau sederhana (dan Anda mungkin terdengar terlalu santai bila memakainya dalam Perfekt).

b.t: Certain dialects (e.g., Bavarian or Swiss or Austrian dialects), in contrast, prefer the Perfekt over the simple past, and younger speakers tend to emphasize the Perfekt as well.
b.t_id: Sebaliknya, dialek tertentu (mis. dialek Bayern, Swiss atau Austria) lebih menyukai Perfekt daripada lampau sederhana, dan penutur muda juga cenderung mengutamakan Perfekt.

b.t: Sein is used as a helping verb when the main verb expresses a change of state in one's physical or mental state, or in one's physical location (and in a few exceptions even when the verb doesn't take an object, and it doesn't describe change: bleiben, sein).

b.t_id: Kasus (Fälle)

b.t: What is a case, you may ask. Good question. In a sentence, the different nouns (or pronouns) have different functions. For example, they can be the subject, the direct object, or the indirect object ... Although nouns in English don't change their shape depending on the role they play in the sentence, in German they do: specifically, they change the article that precedes them; and some nouns add an extra suffix as well.
b.t_id: Apa itu kasus, mungkin Anda bertanya. Pertanyaan bagus. Dalam kalimat, kata benda (atau kata ganti) yang berbeda punya fungsi yang berbeda. Misalnya, kata benda bisa menjadi subjek, objek langsung, atau objek tak langsung ... Dalam bahasa Indonesia bentuk kata benda tidak berubah sesuai perannya dalam kalimat, tetapi dalam bahasa Jerman berubah: khususnya artikel di depannya berubah, dan beberapa kata benda juga mendapat akhiran tambahan.
Nominatif

b.t: The nominative case is used to describe the subject of a sentence. The subject is the main actor in the sentence, the person who carries out an action:
b.t_id: Kasus nominatif dipakai untuk subjek kalimat. Subjek adalah pelaku utama dalam kalimat, orang yang melakukan suatu tindakan:

r: Die sieben Zwerge wohnen in der Dachetage.
The seven dwarves live in the loft apartment.
Die böse Königin wohnt in einem Turm mit einer Hexe.
The evil queen lives in a tower with a witch.

b.t_id: Akusatif

b.t: The accusative case is used to describe the direct object of a sentence. The direct object is the immediate recipient of an action or event:
b.t_id: Kasus akusatif dipakai untuk objek langsung kalimat. Objek langsung adalah penerima langsung suatu tindakan atau kejadian:

r: Die sieben Zwerge haben eine neue Wohnung.
The seven dwarves have a new apartment.
Die alte Hexe macht ein Experiment - ihre arme Katze!
The old witch is doing an experiment - her poor cat!

b.t: The accusative case is also used with a few prepositions: durch, für, gegen, ohne, and um. There will be a handful of prepositions that can either take the accusative or the dative, but they are presented separately under prepositions.
b.t_id: Kasus akusatif juga dipakai bersama beberapa kata depan: durch, für, gegen, ohne, dan um. Ada segelintir kata depan yang bisa memakai akusatif atau datif, tetapi itu dibahas tersendiri di bagian kata depan.

r: Die sieben Zwerge gehen durch den Wald und singen ihr Lieblingslied: hi-ho, hi-ho ...
The seven dwarves are walking through the forest and are singing their favorite song: hi-ho, hi-ho ...
Sie sind ohne Ausnahme für die Umwelt und gegen die Benutzung von Autos, die zu viel Benzin verbrauchen.
They are for the environment and against the use of cars that use too much gas.
Sie arbeiten ohne Maschinen oder Elektrizität.
They work without machines or electricity.
Sie gehen jetzt um einen schönen See herum. He, Hatschi ist in den See gefallen. Kein Wunder, dass er immer niest!
Now they are walking around a pretty lake. Ooops, Sneezy feel into the lake. No wonder that he is always sneezing!

b.t: Finally, the accusative case is used to describe specific times:

r: Die sieben Zwerge wollten den ganzen Nachmittag im Wald verbringen.
The seven dwarves wanted to spend the entire afternoon in the forest.
Sie haben den ganzen Monat auf diesen Ausflug gewartet!
They waited for this outing the entire month!
Aber sie haben nur eine Stunde in der Natur verbringen können! Brummbär ist sehr grantig ...
But they were able to spend only one hour in nature. Grumpy is very grumpy ...

b.t_id: Datif

b.t: The dative case is used to describe the indirect object of a sentence. The indirect object is the recipient of the direct object. In addition to changes in the article, plural nouns also receive an -n suffix (except for nouns that already end in an -n).
b.t_id: Kasus datif dipakai untuk objek tak langsung kalimat. Objek tak langsung adalah penerima objek langsung. Selain perubahan artikel, kata benda jamak juga mendapat akhiran -n (kecuali kata benda yang sudah berakhiran -n).

r: Rotkäppchen bringt der Großmutter eine Flasche Wein und einen frischen Laib Brot.
Little Red Riding Hood brings the grandmother a bottle of wine and a fresh loaf of bread.
Der Wolf zeigt dem kleinen Mädchen seine großen Augen, seine großen Ohren, seinen großen Mund ... und dann frisst er es auf!
The wolf shows the little girl his big eyes, his big ears, his big mouth ... and then he gobbles her up!

b.t: The dative case is also used with some prepositions: aus, außer, bei, mit, nach, seit, von, zu, gegenüber.
b.t_id: Kasus datif juga dipakai bersama beberapa kata depan: aus, außer, bei, mit, nach, seit, von, zu, gegenüber.

Der Wolf ist nach seinem Mittagessen eingeschlafen.

The hunter drags the wolf to the river and cuts open his stomach. Little Red Riding Hood and the grandmother jump out of the wolf's stomach - but the hunter doesn't say anything ... The grandmother doesn't smell so good ...

b.t_id: Genitif

b.t: The genitive case is dying a slow death in the German-speaking countries, especially in spoken language where it is being replaced by the dative case. Nevertheless, it's important for you to know about the genitive case because you will still encounter it in writing.
b.t_id: Kasus genitif perlahan mati di negara-negara berbahasa Jerman, terutama dalam bahasa lisan yang menggantikannya dengan kasus datif. Meski begitu, penting bagi Anda untuk mengenal kasus genitif karena Anda masih akan menemukannya dalam tulisan.

b.t: The genitive case describes possession and can be signaled by an -s suffix at the end of proper nouns or by a change in the article (and an additional -s suffix on masculine and neuter nouns):
b.t_id: Kasus genitif menyatakan kepemilikan dan bisa ditandai akhiran -s di akhir nama diri atau perubahan artikel (dan akhiran -s tambahan pada kata benda maskulin dan netral):

r: The hunter likes Little Red Riding Hood's grandmother!
Kann er das Herz der alten Frau gewinnen?
Can he win the heart of the old woman?
Wird er am Ende des Märchens mit seiner Geliebten bis in alle Ewigkeit zusammen sein?
At the end of the fairy tale, will he be together with his beloved for ever and ever?

b.t: The genitive case is also used with several prepositions: (an)statt, trotz, während, and wegen:
b.t_id: Kasus genitif juga dipakai bersama beberapa kata depan: (an)statt, trotz, während, dan wegen:

r: Nach seiner Erfahrung erzählt Rotkäppchen seiner Mutter, was ihm passiert ist: Mutti, statt meiner Großmutter lag der Wolf im Bett!
After her experience, Little Red Riding Hood tells her mother what happened to her: Mom, instead of my grandmother, the wolf was in the bed!
Die Mutti antwortet dem Mädchen: Und du hast ihn trotz seiner großen Augen, großen Nase und großen Zähnen nicht erkannt?
Her mother answers the little girl: And you didn't recognize him in spite of his big eyes, big nose and big teeth?
Rotkäppchen sagt schluchzend: Mutti, du bist nicht sehr mitfühlend! Wegen der Dunkelheit konnte ich nichts sehen! Es war doch circa 1810 und es gab noch gar keine Elektrizität!
Little Red Riding Hood sobs out: Mom, you are not very sympathetic! Because of the darkness I couldn't see anything! It was, after all, about 1810 and there was no electricity yet!

b.t_id: Kasus: nominatif

b.t: The nominative case is used to describe the subject of a sentence. The subject is the main actor in the sentence, the person who carries out an action:
b.t_id: Kasus nominatif dipakai untuk subjek kalimat. Subjek adalah pelaku utama dalam kalimat, orang yang melakukan suatu tindakan:

r: Die sieben Zwerge wohnen in der Dachetage.
The seven dwarves live in the loft apartment.
Ihre Wohung ist hell und groß. Aber manchmal vermissen die Zwerge ihr altes, romantisches Haus aus dem 19. Jahrhundert.
Their apartment is bright and big. But the dwarves sometimes miss their old, romantic house from the 19th century.
Dort haben die Zwerge ihre geliebte Prinzessin, Schneewittchen, kennen gelernt.
It was there that the dwarves met their beloved princess, Snow White.

b.t: The nominative case is also used to describe predicate nouns (i.e., nouns that are on the other side of verbs such as sein, bleiben, heißen, werden, scheinen from the main subject):
b.t_id: Kasus nominatif juga dipakai untuk kata benda predikat (yaitu kata benda di sisi lain kata kerja seperti sein, bleiben, heißen, werden, scheinen dari subjek utama):

r: Die Prinzessin ist und bleibt die schönste Frau, die die Zwerge sich vorstellen können.
The princess is and remains the most beautiful woman that the dwarves can imagine.
Sie ist auch sehr intelligent; Schneewittchen wird Rechtsanwältin.
She is also very intelligent; Snow White is is going to be (i.e., training to be) a lawyer.

b.t: In the first example, die Prinzessin is the main subject and die schönste Frau is the predicate noun. In the second example, Schneewittchen is the main subject and Rechtsanwältin is the predicate noun.
b.t_id: Dalam contoh pertama, die Prinzessin adalah subjek utama dan die schönste Frau adalah kata benda predikat. Dalam contoh kedua, Schneewittchen adalah subjek utama dan Rechtsanwältin adalah kata benda predikat.

b.t: The biggest trick to being able to use the nominative case (and all four cases, really) is to know the gender of nouns. If you don't know whether Zwerg is masculine, feminine, neuter or plural, the cases can't really fall into place.
b.t_id: Kunci terbesar untuk bisa memakai kasus nominatif (dan sebenarnya keempat kasus) adalah mengetahui jenis kata benda. Jika Anda tidak tahu apakah Zwerg maskulin, feminin, netral atau jamak, kasusnya tidak akan bisa tepat.

b.t: To describe the times of the day, German uses four prepositions: um and gegen for specific times. um is used when an event happens at a particular time, gegen is used to refer to events that happen about a certain time (e.g., noonish). Am is used to describe larger time periods, such as the morning, the afternoon or in the evening. In is used exclusively with Nacht: in der Nacht = at night.
b.t_id: Untuk menyatakan waktu dalam sehari, bahasa Jerman memakai empat kata depan: um dan gegen untuk jam tertentu. um dipakai bila sesuatu terjadi tepat pada jam tertentu, gegen untuk kejadian sekitar jam tertentu (mis. sekitar tengah hari). Am dipakai untuk rentang waktu yang lebih panjang, seperti pagi, siang atau malam. In dipakai khusus dengan Nacht: in der Nacht = pada malam hari.

b.t_id: Kasus: datif

b.t: The dative case is used to describe the indirect object of a sentence. The indirect object is the recipient of the direct object. In addition to changes in the article, plural nouns also receive an -n suffix (except for nouns that already end in an -n).
b.t_id: Kasus datif dipakai untuk objek tak langsung kalimat. Objek tak langsung adalah penerima objek langsung. Selain perubahan artikel, kata benda jamak juga mendapat akhiran -n (kecuali kata benda yang sudah berakhiran -n).

r: Das kleine Mädchen gibt dem alten Mann sein Stückchen Brot.
The little girl gives the old man her* piece of bread.
Es gibt den kleinen Kindern seine Mütze, seinen Rock und sein Hemd.
She gives the little children her hat, her skirt and her shirt.
Gott schenkt dem Mädchen tausende von Talern für ihre Großzügigkeit.

b.t: * Nota Bene: although in English 'little girl' is referred to as 'she,' in German the word 'Mädchen' is grammatically neutral, so the possessive pronoun has to be 'sein' (its). Right now, there are more and more people who would refer to Mädchen as 'sie' (she, her), especially among young people, since they find it insulting to talk about females as 'it.'
b.t_id: * Catatan: kata „Mädchen“ (gadis) dalam bahasa Jerman secara gramatikal netral, jadi kata ganti kepemilikannya harus „sein“. Saat ini makin banyak orang yang merujuk Mädchen dengan „sie“ (dia perempuan), terutama anak muda, karena mereka menganggap tidak sopan menyebut perempuan sebagai „ia/benda“.

b.t: Nevertheless, in formal writing, if the pronoun appears in the same sentence as the word 'Mädchen,' it should be neuter ('es' 'sein', usu.). However, please note that the native speaker narrator used 'ihre Großzügigkeit' in the last sentence instead of 'seine '...
b.t_id: Meski begitu, dalam tulisan resmi, jika kata ganti muncul dalam kalimat yang sama dengan kata „Mädchen“, sebaiknya dipakai bentuk netral („es“, „sein“, dsb.). Namun perhatikan bahwa narator penutur asli memakai „ihre Großzügigkeit“ dalam kalimat terakhir, bukan „seine“...

b.t_id: Kasus: genitif

b.t: The genitive case is dying a slow death in the German-speaking countries, especially in spoken language where it is being replaced by the dative case. Nevertheless, it's important for you to know about the genitive case because you will still encounter it in writing and you will need to be able to recognize it.
b.t_id: Kasus genitif perlahan mati di negara-negara berbahasa Jerman, terutama dalam bahasa lisan yang menggantikannya dengan kasus datif. Meski begitu, penting bagi Anda untuk mengenal kasus genitif karena Anda masih akan menemukannya dalam tulisan dan perlu bisa mengenalinya.
Nama diri

b.t: The genitive case describes possession and can be signaled by an -s suffix at the end of proper nouns, without the apostrophe (like in English: Little Red Riding Hood's).
b.t_id: Kasus genitif menyatakan kepemilikan dan bisa ditandai akhiran -s di akhir nama diri, tanpa apostrof (Rotkäppchens Großmutter = nenek Si Kerudung Merah).

b.t: With any other noun that is not a proper name, the genitive is formed by changing the preceding article; this is also how the accusative or the dative case is indicated. In addition, masculine and neuter nouns receive an -s suffix at the end of the noun. BUT if the masculine or neuter noun is one syllable long, it usually gets an -es.
b.t_id: Untuk kata benda lain yang bukan nama diri, genitif dibentuk dengan mengubah artikel di depannya; begitu pula cara kasus akusatif atau datif ditandai. Selain itu, kata benda maskulin dan netral mendapat akhiran -s di akhir kata benda. TETAPI jika kata benda maskulin atau netral itu bersuku kata satu, biasanya mendapat -es.

b.t_id: Partitif

b.t: When using expressions to describe a part of something (e.g., half of, a quarter of ...), German uses the genitive case. b.t: Conjunctions are typically used either for stylistic purposes (to reduce redundancy or make our speech or writing more fluid) or to help identify closer relationships between ideas. These ideas can be envisioned as two sentences originally, that are combined for stylistic or emphatic reasons. Once they are connected, each original sentence becomes a clause.
b.t_id: Konjungsi biasanya dipakai untuk keperluan gaya bahasa (mengurangi pengulangan atau membuat ucapan dan tulisan lebih lancar) atau untuk menunjukkan hubungan yang lebih erat antargagasan. Gagasan-gagasan ini bisa dibayangkan semula sebagai dua kalimat yang digabung karena alasan gaya atau penekanan. Setelah dihubungkan, setiap kalimat asal menjadi sebuah klausa.

b.t_id: Klausa (Satzteile)

b.t: Conjunctions can connect two different types of clauses:
b.t_id: Konjungsi bisa menghubungkan dua jenis klausa yang berbeda:

b.t: 1. Independent clauses are grammatically complete; that is, they have at least a subject, a verb and all the other words that come with the verb [called complements] such as direct and/or indirect objects. This is true even if there are two of them in the sentence.
b.t_id: 1. Klausa bebas lengkap secara tata bahasa; artinya punya setidaknya subjek, kata kerja dan semua kata lain yang menyertai kata kerja [disebut pelengkap] seperti objek langsung dan/atau tak langsung. Ini berlaku meskipun ada dua klausa bebas dalam satu kalimat.

r: Hänsel und Gretels Vater heiratet eine neue Frau, und das Leben der zwei Kinder wird unerträglich.
Hansel and Gretel's father marries a new woman, and the two children's life becomes impossible.

b.t: 2. Dependent clauses cannot stand on their own and need the support of an independent clause. Although they may have all necessary parts of a sentence (subject, verb, direct object, etc.), they become dependent on another clauses because the subordinating conjunction, which makes the connection between the two sentences stronger and explicit.
b.t_id: 2. Klausa terikat tidak bisa berdiri sendiri dan memerlukan dukungan klausa bebas. Meskipun mungkin punya semua bagian kalimat yang diperlukan (subjek, kata kerja, objek langsung, dll.), klausa ini menjadi bergantung pada klausa lain karena konjungsi subordinatif, yang membuat hubungan kedua kalimat lebih erat dan tegas.

b.t_id: Konjungsi koordinatif (Koordinierende Konjunktionen)

b.t: Coordinating conjunctions join equal clauses: either two independent clauses or two dependent clauses. The word order stays the same in each clause, with the verb in second position.
b.t_id: Konjungsi koordinatif menghubungkan klausa yang setara: dua klausa bebas atau dua klausa terikat. Susunan kata di setiap klausa tetap sama, dengan kata kerja di posisi kedua.

b.t: Subordinating conjunctions join unequal clauses: one independent and one dependent clause. The word order in the independent clause is the regular verb-in-second-position; the word order in the dependent clause changes, however, and the conjugated verb goes to the end of the clause

b.t: In German there are two main ways to express negation: by using the adverb nicht (not) or the indefinite article kein (no, not a, not any). However, nicht and kein are not interchangeable.
b.t_id: Dalam bahasa Jerman ada dua cara utama untuk menyatakan negasi: dengan kata keterangan nicht (tidak) atau artikel tak tentu kein (bukan, tidak ada, tidak satu pun). Namun nicht dan kein tidak bisa saling dipertukarkan.
Kein

b.t: Kein is used to negate a noun that would otherwise be preceded by an indefinite article or by no article at all. It may be helpful for you to think of kein as the exact opposite of the indefinite article ein.
b.t_id: Kein dipakai untuk menegasikan kata benda yang semestinya didahului artikel tak tentu atau tanpa artikel sama sekali. Mungkin membantu jika Anda menganggap kein sebagai kebalikan persis dari artikel tak tentu ein.

b.t: Because kein is a type of article, it is used specifically with nouns. In contrast, nicht is an adverb, so it is used to modify many different parts of language, including: verbs, adjectives, other adverbs, prepositions, phrases, clauses, and sentences. A good rule of thumb is to use nicht whenever you can't use kein.

b.t: Coordinating conjunctions join equal clauses: either two independent clauses or two dependent clauses. The word order stays the same in each clause, with the verb in second position.

b.t: There are two types of word order that you should see with subordinating conjunctions:
b.t_id: Ada dua jenis susunan kata yang perlu Anda kenali dengan konjungsi subordinatif:

b.t: 1. Independent clause first, dependent clause second. In this case, the conjugated verb in the independent clause is in the second position, while the conjugated verb in the dependent clause goes to the end of that clause.
b.t_id: 1. Klausa bebas dulu, klausa terikat kemudian. Dalam hal ini kata kerja terkonjugasi dalam klausa bebas berada di posisi kedua, sedangkan kata kerja terkonjugasi dalam klausa terikat pindah ke akhir klausa itu.

r: Gretel stößt die Hexe in den Backofen, damit sie ihren Bruder retten kann.

b.t: 2. Dependent clause first, independent clause second. In this case, the conjugated verb in the dependent clause still goes to the end of that clause, but the conjugated verb in the independent clause comes 'first' (it is actually still second position, because the entire dependent clause fills the first slot).
b.t_id: 2. Klausa terikat dulu, klausa bebas kemudian. Dalam hal ini kata kerja terkonjugasi dalam klausa terikat tetap pindah ke akhir klausanya, tetapi kata kerja terkonjugasi dalam klausa bebas muncul „pertama“ (sebenarnya tetap di posisi kedua, karena seluruh klausa terikat mengisi posisi pertama).

b.t: Word order (also called syntax) in German is usually driven by the placement of the verb. The verb in German can be in the second position (most common), initial position (verb first), and clause-final position.
b.t_id: Susunan kata (disebut juga sintaksis) dalam bahasa Jerman biasanya ditentukan oleh letak kata kerja. Kata kerja dalam bahasa Jerman bisa berada di posisi kedua (paling umum), posisi pertama (kata kerja di depan), dan posisi akhir klausa.

b.t: The finite verb in second position
b.t_id: Kata kerja terkonjugasi di posisi kedua

b.t: The most basic word order in German, just like in English, is the subject-verb-direct object sequence:

b.t_id: Seperti terlihat, kata kerja terkonjugasi berada di posisi kedua di setiap kalimat. Inilah posisi dasar yang paling umum bagi kata kerja terkonjugasi.

b.t: The finite verb in clause-final position
b.t_id: Kata kerja terkonjugasi di akhir klausa

b.t: In a few instances, the finite verb can also be at the end of a clause, at the end of the dependent clause. This happens when the clause is introduced by a subordinating conjunction (e.g., weil, ob, nachdem).
b.t_id: Dalam beberapa keadaan, kata kerja terkonjugasi juga bisa berada di akhir klausa, di akhir klausa terikat. Ini terjadi bila klausa diawali konjungsi subordinatif (mis. weil, ob, nachdem).
a) konjungsi subordinatif

b.t: Typically (unless it's during an ongoing oral discussion), subordinating conjunctions are part of a larger sentence that also has a main (independent) clause. The dependent clause, the one introduced by the subordinating conjunction, explains or expands or modifies the information presented in the independent clause. The subordinate clause can precede or follow the independent clause.
b.t_id: Biasanya (kecuali dalam diskusi lisan yang sedang berlangsung), konjungsi subordinatif menjadi bagian dari kalimat yang lebih besar yang juga punya klausa utama (bebas). Klausa terikat, yang diawali konjungsi subordinatif, menjelaskan, memperluas atau mengubah informasi dalam klausa bebas. Klausa terikat bisa mendahului atau menyusul klausa bebas.

b.t: There will be a finite verb in each clause. The finite verb of the independent clause will be in second position. The finite verb of the dependent clause will be in the clause-final position.
b.t_id: Setiap klausa punya kata kerja terkonjugasi. Kata kerja terkonjugasi klausa bebas berada di posisi kedua. Kata kerja terkonjugasi klausa terikat berada di akhir klausa.

r: Ich hoffe, dass sie bald in den Apfel beißt! Ich kann kaum warten, bis sie stirbt!
I hope that she takes a bite of the apple soon! I can hardly wait until she dies!

b.t: Each sentence begins with the independent (main) clause. The first position is occupied by the subject 'ich' (in both sentences), and the second position by the finite verb of the independent clause 'hoffe' and 'kann'.
b.t_id: Setiap kalimat diawali klausa bebas (utama). Posisi pertama diisi subjek „ich“ (di kedua kalimat), dan posisi kedua oleh kata kerja terkonjugasi klausa bebas „hoffe“ dan „kann“.

b.t: After the comma comes the subordinate clause, introduced by the subordinating conjunction dass and bis. The finite verb of the subordinate clause, beisst and stirbt are in clause-final position.
b.t_id: Sesudah koma muncul anak kalimat, diawali konjungsi subordinatif dass dan bis. Kata kerja terkonjugasi anak kalimat, beisst dan stirbt, berada di akhir klausa.

b.t: Contrast this arrangement with the following example, in which the dependent clause begins the sentence:
b.t_id: Bandingkan susunan ini dengan contoh berikut, yang kalimatnya diawali klausa terikat:

r: Nachdem du meinen Apfel gegessen hast, willst du nie wieder irgendwas anderes essen! Haha!
After you eat my apple, you will not want to eat anything else ever again! Haha!

b.t: This sentence begins with the subordinate clause (introduced by the subordinating conjunction nachdem). The finite verb gegessen hast is in the clause-final position, immediately preceding the comma that separates the dependent and independent clauses.
b.t_id: Kalimat ini diawali anak kalimat (dengan konjungsi subordinatif nachdem). Kata kerja terkonjugasi gegessen hast berada di akhir klausa, tepat sebelum koma yang memisahkan klausa terikat dan klausa bebas.

b.t: The second clause is the independent clause. The finite verb willst is in the second position; the first position of the sentence is occupied by the entire subordinate clause!
b.t_id: Klausa kedua adalah klausa bebas. Kata kerja terkonjugasi willst berada di posisi kedua; posisi pertama kalimat diisi seluruh anak kalimat!
b) anak kalimat relatif

b.t: The effect of relative pronouns is the same as the subordinating conjunctions: the finite verb goes to the end of the clause that is introduced by the relative pronoun.
b.t_id: Pengaruh kata ganti relatif sama dengan konjungsi subordinatif: kata kerja terkonjugasi pindah ke akhir klausa yang diawali kata ganti relatif.

b.t: Finite verbs can be replaced by modal verbs (which, as the name suggests, modify the meaning of the former main verb). As a result of the incoming modal verb (which is conjugated, and is the new finite verb), the original verb turns into an infinitive.
b.t_id: Kata kerja terkonjugasi bisa digantikan kata kerja modal (yang, sesuai namanya, mengubah makna kata kerja utama sebelumnya). Akibat hadirnya kata kerja modal (yang dikonjugasikan dan menjadi kata kerja terkonjugasi yang baru), kata kerja asli berubah menjadi infinitif.

Dengan haben/sein dan hätte/wäre, kata kerja asli menjadi partisip. Dengan werden, menjadi infinitif.

b.t: Adjectives describe nouns, and can either precede or follow the noun in German without affecting the meaning of the article. In German, just like English, adjectives can be graded to express comparisons between two (comparative) or more (comparative and superlative) things, places, people or thoughts. Unlike in English, however, adjectives that precede nouns take endings depending on the case, gender and number of that noun.

Komparatif dan superlatif

b.t: Adjectives can be graded to express comparative and superlative qualities.

r: Aschenputtels Leben wurde viel schlimmer, als sein Vater die andere Frau heiratete.

Das arme Mädchen wurde jeden Tag immer trauriger.
The poor girl was sadder and sadder every day.
Als der Vater von einer Reise zurückkam, brachte er den Stiefschwestern die schönsten Kleider, Perlen und Edelsteine mit.

b.t_id: III. Akhiran kata sifat

b.t: Attributive adjectives (the ones preceding the noun they describe) can take three different types of endings, depending on what precedes them:
b.t_id: Kata sifat atributif (yang mendahului kata benda yang digambarkannya) bisa mendapat tiga jenis akhiran yang berbeda, tergantung apa yang mendahuluinya:

b.t: a) adjectives after definite articles or der-words
b.t_id: a) kata sifat sesudah artikel tentu atau kata-der

b.t: When an adjective comes between a definite article or der-word and the noun it modifies, it takes weak adjective endings (because the article already gives enough grammatical information to signal the noun's gender, case and number).
b.t_id: Bila kata sifat berada di antara artikel tentu atau kata-der dan kata benda yang digambarkannya, ia mendapat akhiran lemah (karena artikelnya sudah cukup memberi informasi gramatikal tentang jenis, kasus dan jumlah kata benda).

r: Das kleine Aschenputtel wollte nur einen Zweig von einem Haselbusch; sie pflanzt den Zweig auf das Grab ihrer Mutter.
The little Cinderella wanted only a twig from a hazel bush; she plants the twig on the tomb of her mother.
Der schöne Baum ist der einzige Trost für das arme Mädchen.
The beautiful tree is the only consolation for the poor little girl.

b.t: b) adjectives preceded by indefinite articles or ein-words
b.t_id: b) kata sifat yang didahului artikel tak tentu atau kata-ein

b.t: Adjectives that are preceded by an indefinite article (ein, eine, keine) or other ein-words (meine, deine, seine) receive strong endings because the article does not give enough grammatical information to signal the noun's gender, case and number.
b.t_id: Kata sifat yang didahului artikel tak tentu (ein, eine, keine) atau kata-ein lain (meine, deine, seine) mendapat akhiran kuat karena artikelnya tidak cukup memberi informasi gramatikal tentang jenis, kasus dan jumlah kata benda.

r: Ein weißes Vöglein kam jeden Tag zum Baum.
A white bird came to the tree every day.
Im Reich gab es einen alten König.
In the realm there was an old King.
Er arrangierte ein großes Fest für seinen Sohn, um für ihn eine Frau zu finden.
He arranged a large feast for his son, in order to find him a wife.

b.t_id: c) kata sifat tanpa pendahulu

b.t: Then there are some adjectives that are either not preceded by any determiners or are preceded by quantifiers such as many (viele), some (einige) or few (wenige). These adjectives take a different set of strong endings to compensate for the lacking grammatical information about the noun's gender, case and number.
b.t_id: Lalu ada kata sifat yang tidak didahului kata penentu apa pun atau didahului kata penunjuk jumlah seperti viele (banyak), einige (beberapa) atau wenige (sedikit). Kata sifat ini mendapat seperangkat akhiran kuat lain untuk menggantikan informasi gramatikal tentang jenis, kasus dan jumlah kata benda yang tidak ada.

Aber zwei weiße Täubchen kamen zu Aschenputtel und brachten ihm goldene und silberne Kleider, und es ging aufs Fest.

Aschenputtel lief weg, aber verlor ihren Schuh. Nach einigen falschen Versuchen findet der Prinz seine Braut und heiratet sie.

b.t_id: IV. Tanpa deklinasi

b.t: There are a numbers of adjectives, mostly colors and foreign loan words, that do not take adjective endings. Interestingly, they also do not exist in comparative and superlative forms.
b.t_id: Ada sejumlah kata sifat, kebanyakan warna dan kata serapan asing, yang tidak mendapat akhiran kata sifat. Menariknya, kata-kata itu juga tidak punya bentuk komparatif dan superlatif.

b.t: Regular comparative and superlative adjectives merely put an -er and an -est ending on the basic adjective, even if they are very long (in contrast to English, which uses 'more' or 'most' if the adjective is more than two syllables long, such as diligent or intelligent). In the column 'superlative' the first version (e.g., 'die böste') is the attributive adjective, while the second version (e.g., 'am bösesten) is the predicate adjective. Remember: 'the most evil queen' is an attributive adjective and 'this queen was the most evil' is a predicate adjective.
b.t_id: Kata sifat komparatif dan superlatif yang beraturan cukup menambahkan akhiran -er dan -est pada kata sifat dasar, sepanjang apa pun kata sifat itu (bahasa Jerman tidak memakai kata tambahan seperti „lebih“ dan „paling“). Dalam kolom „superlatif“, bentuk pertama (mis. „die böseste“) adalah kata sifat atributif, sedangkan bentuk kedua (mis. „am bösesten“) adalah kata sifat predikatif. Ingat: „ratu paling jahat“ adalah kata sifat atributif dan „ratu ini paling jahat“ adalah kata sifat predikatif.
